title: A timely SNAP theft report can be denied after a form-process failure and corrected on appeal without public proof of replacement receipt
source_unit: Connecticut DSS/OLCRAH Notice of Decision, Request No. 235520
geography: Connecticut SNAP household; Connecticut Department of Social Services administrative hearing

observations.period: 2024 administrative decision; transaction, report, hearing, and order dates redacted in the public PDF

denominator.unit: anonymized OLCRAH administrative case; not a replacement-rate or household-outcome denominator

stolen_amount.unit: U.S. dollars in four unauthorized out-of-state SNAP transactions

route_and_timing.value: The one-person SNAP household discovered the loss after an attempted $208.73 purchase was declined, reported it three days later, received a replacement card, and submitted the replacement form 32 days after discovery
route_and_timing.unit: reported administrative sequence; exact dates redacted

initial_decision.value: DSS denied replacement on the ground that the theft was not reported within 30 days, although the hearing record found the initial report occurred three days after discovery and the agency did not document when it issued the required form
initial_decision.unit: reported agency decision and hearing finding

corrective_response.value: The appeal was granted; DSS was ordered to rescind the denial and process the replacement request as timely

receipt_and_adequacy.unit: missing post-order issuance, account credit, food purchases, interim food access, bills, debt, adequacy, later continuity, recurrence, trust, action, and exit

mechanism.value: A recipient can meet the initial reporting window yet lose access to replacement through an undocumented form-delivery and submission clock; a hearing can correct the administrative disposition without exposing whether the corrected remedy reaches the account or restores food access

observations.method: Structured extraction from the official Connecticut OLCRAH decision; transaction history, appellant testimony, agency process, denial, hearing correction, and downstream non-observation are kept separate.
observations.uncertainty: The public decision anonymizes the appellant and redacts dates. It does not publish the post-order processing result, account credit, food purchases, interim substitution, adequacy, later continuity, or household recovery.
observations.subgroup: One anonymized Connecticut SNAP household; no population denominator or comparison group is supplied.
observations.counterinterpretation: The corrective order may have produced a timely replacement and prevented a durable food gap, or the household may have remained without usable benefits; the public record ends before either outcome is observed.

boundary: This record establishes one anonymized Connecticut administrative case through a granted corrective order. It does not establish post-order replacement issuance, recipient receipt, benefit adequacy, food security, household recovery, population rates, durable trust, action, or exit.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The hash covers the published administrative decision; identifying fields, raw EBT transactions, and household follow-up records are not retained.
